item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Mathematical Models for Geopolitical and Cyber Risks (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-18 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/STAT-04 Metodi matematici dell'economia e delle scienze attuariali e finanziarie

The project defines a unified quantitative framework for the stochastic modeling, financial valuation, and mitigation of emerging risks (geopolitical and cyber). International crisis impacts are formalized using econometric indices (text-mining and new robust indicators) and jump processes, distinguishing between geopolitical threats and events. This framework integrates cyber risk via stochastic processes capturing potential interdependence and cross-contagion between physical and digital domains, aiming at the fair pricing of parametric hedges in incomplete markets and dynamic mitigation via stochastic control. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Local Mapping of Expenditure on Social Care Interventions (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-03 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/ECON-06 Economia aziendale

The project analyzes and maps public expenditure on social assistance in Italy to reconstruct its territorial distribution and examine how national and local welfare measures interact. In recent years, non-contributory assistance spending, including income support, disability benefits, family allowances, and measures addressing poverty and social exclusion, has increased rapidly, exceeding €180 billion in 2024. The research will systematically map the main assistance programs, defining a consistent set of comparable interventions and analyzing their distribution at least at the NUTS 2 level. The objective is to identify complementarities, overlaps, and fragmentation across policy…

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-15 23:59
Institution: Univ. Bocconi MILANO, Milano
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/ECON-01 Economia politica

The project examines how public opinion forms on specific issues and European integration. Its empirical research will analyze data from sample surveys, questionnaires, and experiments, alongside parliamentary and committee debates, to identify the arguments used and the logical structure of the texts. The Research Appointee will help collect, organize, and analyze quantitative and textual data. Their work will include supporting experiments; analyzing political speeches, editorials, and newspaper articles, including with AI tools; and assisting with statistical and econometric analyses.
